what: MODS_A2 A25 -- the multiply's EX occupancy cut from 4 cycles to 3. The memory image is BYTE-IDENTICAL to bench_a23.mem and the only source difference from A23's build is MULDIV_MUL_CYCLES, so every delta below is one-variable.
clock_note: 70.000 MHz, not A23's 74.576.  The A25 netlist misses A23's clock by 0.423 ns on the core's writeback-to-PC redirect path, which the multiplier is not on.  Cycle counts and IPC do not depend on the clock and are directly comparable with A23; the derived rates are not.  A28 measures Fmax properly.
flags: -march=rv32im_zba_zbb_zbs_zbkb_zicond_zicsr -mabi=ilp32 -O2 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostartfiles -fno-common -Wall | dhrystone: -std=gnu89 + upstream no-inline pragma | mul/div: hardware M extension

vs_a23.note: ZERO change in every counter.  exstall is 66,000,000 = 2,000,000 x 33, which is one DIVIDE per run and NO multiplies: at -march=rv32imb the compiler strength-reduces Dhrystone's multiply into Zba shift-adds, so A21 had already removed what A25 makes cheaper.
The cycle saving and the exstall reduction are the SAME number, 23,490,000, which is exactly the multiply count implied by A23's exstall/3.  CoreMark performs no divides at all.

2,688 multiplies in the rv32im NTT, one cycle each.  The rv32i build is unchanged because it contains no MUL instruction at all -- libgcc multiplies in software.  MODS_A2 3.6 P1 arriving as pre-committed: the software NTT baseline got FASTER, so 10 M2's reported coprocessor speedup gets SMALLER.  That is the correct direction.
